pos.text: This is the best incremental game out in my opinion. I have no critiques. I simply desire more content, which is a good problem to have. The game far exceeds its price. Great job by the Dev. Thank you for the pleasant experience.

There's some seriously innovative stuff here.  Other incremental games don't have the sense of story that Increlution has, and the user interface is extremely clean and surprisingly powerful.  I have 15 hours logged, and maybe 10 hours of genuine activity.  With the status screen telling me that I've seen 5.9% of the content, this has been one of the most cost-effective games I've bought.  And let's face it, I play incremental games: that means I'm obsessed with resource efficiency.

Dev is sick, so the next update might take a while longer to drop. - Check the game's discord for updates

Really good game though, and for the current price it has way more content than one could expect even from a lot of more expensive "finished" games on the market right now.

There's no reason not to get it imo

I've played this game so much it's insane and i still feel like i haven't had enough. This game is the perfect balance of story telling, exponential growth, and the right amount of idle and interactive. Highly recommend playing it
Best idle game, you get to see howmuch seconds you were faster then last run at each stage, you also get to decide the order of doing things in depth opening up for a lot of min maxing
Best Incremental game I've seen. Balanced, clear UI, immersion and also some funny moments.
Great game not finished but still a lot of content

I am so sorry that it took me so long to write a review. I really adore this game and what it reminds me of - very old single player text adventure games but so much more interesting. It's hard to appreciate it this way if you've never experienced them. This game has a nuance to it that you either love or hate and that's why I took so long to review it. God bless.
Fun incremental game with quite a bit of content.  Does tend to get tedious towards the end but still good for a game that was abandoned.  Too bad.

This is SUPER niche, but it's an amazing game and the pacing is perfect. There was never a run where I didn't feel like the tension was absolutely dialed in. Somehow it's so simple yet so deep. Perfection.
After completing *check notes* early acces. Dare i say, i like it
I love this game; I haven't played many like it, and the ones I have I didn't like as much.

This review is based on the game as is, future updates are never garunteed.

Try the demo. The rest of the game is more of the same. 
There is a tiny sprinkle of strategy and 'builds' as you get near the end of the 220-250 hour game, but nothing crazy.
I thought I would put it down after getting to the end, but I guess I liked it enough I'm doing NG+ and enjoying it again.
Try the demo.
Super fun game to have in the background only requiring input every 20 minutes or so.

I really don't know why this game is so addictive, but it is. 
I've been playing it for 3 hours and made very little progress, and I don't see that changing anytime soon.
But, do you know when you are so fed up with life and so overwhelmed that anything that requires more than 1% of brain activity is not bearable?
This is for those days (months? years?).
Amazing game, just hope for the developer to get well and hopfully finish the big update soon

Despite the fact the game has been abandoned, it has exciting gameplay, a nice logical plot, and sufficient depth in its current state.

The developer is seriously ill. And instead of accusing him of all his sins, blame a specific country. Country that, for political reasons, hid the truth about the leak of a deadly disease from a biolab.

Great "Time Loop" game in the vein of Progress Knight.

For those into the kind of "go as far as your can, die, get a bit stronger passively for next time" gameloop with little bits of strategy and discovery.

If looking for something similar I recommend Terraformental, which is on steam now.

In any case this game is certainly worth the price. It's unfortunate the dev's progress was halted due to long covid (last developer update was December of 2025, saying as much). Even if a new patch is never delivered the game as is has plenty of life to it and is worth the price.

Cool idle game and cool concept for 4€, keeps your entertained for a while, pursuing the mysteries and going further each time you start your journey again.
It's sad that the dev doesn't update it anymore, i'm hoping for a sequel !
its fine but lack of development is a bit of a put down but uptoo the end and prestige running up to content is fun, hope we get the new chapters eventually that was promissed
Game is really addictive. I wish it was less Idler, but I still can't stop playing
Really good game and if you feel like its too short the NG+ perks allow you to replay it indefinitely. Can't wait for the next chapters
Fun idle game to run in the background.
unique active idle game
its pretty good

neg.text:
It has been three years since the last update. This game has a cool concept for an incremental game, an actually unique one versus the cookie cutter ones you get these days with unity store asset flips.

Unfortunately it is incomplete, and after three years of no updates to the game it's clear to anyone that is how it will remain. I leave this simply as a warning for potential buyers.

Game is terminally in EA.
Too long has passed since last story update and i feel i have to warn potential buyers the story is incomplete and probably will never be finished.
Can't reccomend.

It was a good game progression was good and steady and it always felt like progress was being made. However the game has been abandoned by the dev, i suggest you save ur money and find something else. Don't believe the dev notes that were posted about progress. No progress has been made, 4+ years since update, it's obvious it is no longer being worked on. Still it will give you a few hours of fun, and what is there was very well done. So try it at your own risk.
abandoned :/ like my love for it.

Game is very, very repetitive, with very few decisions to make (none of them seem really impactful, or seem to be a lot more optimized)
- Start a run, wait a bit (15m+)
- Click a button or two, wait a minute
- Click another button or two, wait a few minutes
- reset

This really isn't much of a game - more of a tech demo.  There are few, if any, real decisions to make.  Beyond the first chapter, the game is pure repetition with increasingly longer time increments before anything resembling a decision arises.

I wish there was a 'meh' option instead of having to choose thumbs up or down. 

Increlution isn't a terrible game, but it's also not for everyone. The incremental nature of it fulfils some primitive urge to see numbers go up and progress get made every time you reincarnate. But it's an awfully dull game which ENCOURAGES you to walk away and do other things - the game has the option to make a sound to tell you to come back when it needs you to do something! That means that the hours and hours people have playing this game really represents far less time of GAMEPLAY and more of having the game run in the background.

There's also a lot of wasted opportunity here. There is no real plot to the game! You wake up and start moving to avoid dying of hunger, then take more or less random decisions as you travel. Only by the end of chapter 5 do you get a hint of a plot happening - and that to

Sadly, an abandoned game, just before the great promised update.
Shame, really; it was pretty decent, even if tedious to get through.
Meaningless meta progression unfortunately. Only a multiplier, meaning you only need to click things in order to progress, no thinking no planning.

I think I have a love-hate relationship with this game, and that's probably got a lot to do with the play style.  I'll probaby keep trying to progress for a bit because I struggle to walk away from any story once I've started.  That said, the way this game is built feels pretty repetitive.  I think maybe having some illustrations pop up to go along with each piece of the story as it unlocks might help a bit with immersion?  I'd say this game is probably best suited for those with the patience for grinding.  If you're more the type to look for consistent story flow this might not be your ideal game.  Credit where credit is due, it is very accessible for those of us with limited gaming experience.
I don't usually review games, but this game sucks, its terrible game mechanism.
